terms.definition: A living organism of its own kingdom - mushrooms, mold, and yeast - neither plant nor animal.
terms.function: Absorbs food and reproduces with spores.
terms.whereItIs: In soil, on wood, and on our skin and in our gut.
terms.whyItMatters: Fungi are key decomposers and are all around us.

terms.definition: The tiny thread-like cells that spread from a fungus and make up its mycelium.
terms.function: Spread through food/soil absorbing nutrients and dissolving food.
terms.whereItIs: Running under the surface of what the fungus colonizes.
terms.whyItMatters: They are the working arms that feed the whole fungus.

terms.definition: The whole tangled network of hyphae - the main, often hidden body of a fungus.
terms.function: The food-absorbing body of the fungus spreads through soil or wood.
terms.whereItIs: Underneath the ground where you see a mushroom.
terms.whyItMatters: It is the part you usually do not see, but is the real fungus.

terms.definition: A tiny spec released by a fungus that can grow into a new fungus.
terms.function: Reproduces and spreads the fungus to new places.
terms.whereItIs: Made and released from the mushroom fruiting body.
terms.whyItMatters: Spores are how fungi create the next generation.
